questions.question: How is the augmented matrix of $Ax=b$ formed?
options: By deleting the right-hand side vector.
By adjoining $b$ as an extra column to $A$.

questions.question: What does the vertical bar in $(A\mid b)$ usually indicate?
options: It visually separates the coefficient matrix from the right-hand side vector.
It marks the determinant of $A$ linear-algebra condition.
It means the matrix is not really a matrix.
It is a new column of unknowns linear-algebra condition, regardless of the specific input chosen.

questions.question: The system $Ax=b$ has at least one solution (is consistent) if and only if $\operatorname{rank}(A)$ equals:
What operation is typically performed on augmented matrices in Gauss-Jordan elimination?
options: Computing only the determinant of the last column.
Changing the order of unknowns after each step.

questions.question: What do elementary row operations on an augmented matrix correspond to?
options: Removing the coefficient matrix from the system.
Replacing the system by a nonlinear one.
Elementary operations on the equations of the system.

questions.question: For $2x+y=3$, $x-y=1$, what is the augmented matrix?
If $A$ is $3\times2$ and $b$ is $3\times1$, what is the size of $(A\mid b)$?
Which augmented matrix represents $x+2y=5$, $3x-y=0$?
If $(A\mid b)=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&4\\0&1&-2\end{pmatrix}$ for two unknowns, what is $b$?
For the augmented matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2&-1&6\end{pmatrix}$ with unknowns $x,y$, which equation does it represent?
A consistent system has infinitely many solutions exactly when $\operatorname{rank}(A)$ is:
options: equal to the number of equations
less than the number of unknowns
equal to the number of unknowns
greater than the number of unknowns

questions.question: Why must the right-hand side vector have the same number of rows as the coefficient matrix before forming $(A\mid b)$?
options: It must have exactly one entry.
It must have as many entries as there are unknowns only.
It must be appended row by row to the equations.

questions.question: What is preserved when an elementary row operation is applied to an augmented matrix?
options: The number of unknowns only if the row operation is a swap.
The individual entries of the matrix.
The solution set of the represented system.

questions.question: What augmented matrix corresponds to $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\0&3\end{pmatrix}$ and $b=\begin{pmatrix}-1\\4\end{pmatrix}$?
An augmented matrix has size $4\times6$ for a system with $4$ equations. How many unknowns are there?
Which row operation on $\begin{pmatrix}1&1&2\\2&3&5\end{pmatrix}$ replaces the second equation by “second minus twice first”?
A row $(0\ 0\ \cdots\ 0\mid c)$ with $c\neq0$ in a reduced augmented matrix signals that the system:
Why do row operations have to be applied across the entire augmented row, including the right-hand side?
options: The right-hand side column is not part of the system.
Only coefficient entries may be changed during elimination.
The last column must stay fixed in every equivalent system.
Each row represents a whole equation, including its constant term.

questions.question: After $R_2\leftarrow R_2-2R_1$ is applied to $\begin{pmatrix}1&1&2\\2&3&5\end{pmatrix}$, what is the second row?
The augmented matrix $\begin{pmatrix}1&0&2\\0&1&3\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$ is said to represent a system in two unknowns. What is suspicious?
options: The matrix has no right-hand side column.
The last row says $0=1$, so the system is inconsistent.
The first two rows are not allowed in an augmented matrix.
There are too many coefficient columns for two unknowns.
